title: Tesla Roadster with SpaceX thrusters
what: Tesla unveiled the long-delayed Roadster outside Waco, Texas, nine years after the 2017 prototype. Its top trims use SpaceX-developed cold-gas thrusters to leap, flip and land. No price; Musk says production starts in 2028.
quip: Actual rocket science, pointed at last at a car park.
cost: Reservations of $50,000 (Performance) or $250,000 (Thrust); no price announced. Deposits were first taken in 2017.

sources.title: Tesla unveils Cyberfied new Roadster that can kickflip
Tesla reveals SpaceX-powered Roadster that flies and falls with style
Tesla is unveiling the new Roadster for real this time, promise

title: Friend 2.0 pendant
what: An always-listening AI companion necklace, relaunched with a speaker so it can talk back. It costs $249, up from $129, and remembering anything beyond 30 days requires a monthly subscription of about $10.
quip: A friend who is always listening, now on a subscription plan.
cost: $249 per pendant. The company earlier spent $1.8M on the friend.com domain and over $1M on New York subway ads.

sources.title: That AI wearable you don't like just got worse
AI startup Friend spent more than $1M on all those subway ads
AI 'Friend' Company Spent $1.8 Million and Most of Its Funds on Domain Name

title: BF Island
what: At SXSW, BuzzFeed presented new consumer AI apps as a source of revenue, including BF Island, a group chat where users recreate meme trends with AI-edited photos.
quip: The future of media: a group chat of AI-edited memes.

sources.title: BuzzFeed debuts AI slop apps in bid for new revenue

title: AI.com Super Bowl launch
what: Crypto.com CEO Kris Marszalek launched AI.com, a platform for building personal AI agents, with a 30-second ad during Super Bowl LX. The website crashed under the traffic.
quip: Seventy million dollars for two letters, and the website still fell over.
cost: About $70M, paid in crypto, reportedly spent on the AI.com domain

sources.title: Crypto.com CEO Kris Marszalek bought AI.com for $70 million in crypto, plans Super Bowl debut

title: Moltbook
what: A Reddit-style social network where only AI agents post, comment and upvote, while humans may watch. Meta bought it in March 2026 and moved its founders into Meta Superintelligence Labs.
quip: Doomscrolling, now fully automated. Humans welcome to observe.

sources.title: Humans welcome to observe: This social network is for AI agents only

title: Project AVA hologram companion
what: A desk tube that projects a 5.5-inch animated AI avatar, running on xAI's Grok at launch, to chat, coach gamers and help with schedules. Razer took $20 reservations, with shipping planned for the second half of 2026.
quip: Companionship, now sold by the tube. USB-C cable included.
cost: $20 reservation deposit; final price not announced

sources.title: Project AVA: The Next Evolution of AI Companions
Razer put a waifu in a bottle at CES 2026

title: Fridge with Google Gemini
what: Samsung announced the first refrigerator with Google Gemini: built-in cameras identify the food inside and suggest recipes. At the CES 2026 demo, it could not see items in the door shelves or the freezer.
quip: A large language model, at last confirming that you are out of milk.

sources.title: Samsung To Unveil AI Vision Built With Google Gemini at CES 2026
Google Gemini recognizes what leftover food is still in the Samsung refrigerator

title: Sora app
what: A TikTok-style social app where every video is AI-generated, including 'cameos' of users themselves. It hit the top of the US App Store; in March 2026 OpenAI said it would discontinue the app.
quip: Six months, one Disney deal, then: "We're saying goodbye to Sora."
cost: Disney agreed in Dec 2025 to invest $1B in OpenAI and license 200+ characters for Sora; it exited the deal after the shutdown.

sources.title: OpenAI Releases Social App for Sharing AI Videos From Sora

title: Vibes
what: A short-form video feed in the Meta AI app made entirely of AI-generated clips, which users can create, remix and cross-post to Instagram and Facebook. Meta began testing it as a standalone app in February 2026.
quip: Reels, minus the inconvenience of anything having happened.

sources.title: Meta launches 'Vibes,' a short-form video feed of AI slop
Meta tests a stand-alone app for its AI-generated 'Vibes' videos

title: Optimus serving popcorn at the Tesla Diner
what: Tesla opened a 24-hour retro diner and drive-in cinema with EV chargers in Hollywood. On opening day, an Optimus humanoid robot scooped popcorn into bags for guests and waved.
quip: Humanoid robotics reaches its first commercial milestone: popcorn.

sources.title: Tesla Diner: Photos show opening of Musk's futuristic California drive-in
Fans wait for hours to visit Tesla diner and drive-in movie theater in Hollywood on opening day

title: Humane AI Pin
what: A $699 screenless AI wearable pitched as a smartphone alternative. Humane sold its technology and most staff to HP and switched the pins off on 28 February 2025, ten days after the announcement.
quip: The future of computing, with ten days' notice.
cost: Humane raised $230M; HP paid $116M for its technology and staff, not the Pin
